query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight high-entropy alloy sintered at 1000 °C (LW1000) exhibits superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared to its lower sintering temperature variants because the high-temperature processing promotes surface enrichment of Al and Fe and the in situ formation of a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide film that serves as a robust passive barrier.
generation.material_initial_state: Nanocrystalline BCC solid-solution precursor powders of a MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight HEA produced by mechanical alloying.
generation.intervention: Spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C (designated as LW1000).
generation.conditions: Exposed to high-temperature environments and corrosive media (e.g., 3.5 wt% NaCl solution) where the combined effects of elevated temperature and tribological wear (tribo-corrosion) are present.
generation.structural_mediator: Surface enrichment of Al and Fe leading to the formation of a continuous spinel-type oxide passive film.
generation.mechanism: High sintering temperature induces element segregation at the surface, facilitating the in situ formation of a dense protective oxide layer. This layer shifts the corrosion mechanism from a direct metal/solution attack to a diffusion-controlled process, thereby reducing ion penetration during combined mechanical wear and corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: The LW1000 alloy will display a significantly higher passive film resistance (at least one order of magnitude greater) and a lower corrosion current density, resulting in enhanced tribo-corrosion resistance relative to variants sintered at lower temperatures.
generation.baseline: HEA samples sintered at lower temperatures (850–950 °C) or conventional structural alloys under similar tribo-corrosion test conditions.
generation.boundary: The improved performance is expected when the protective oxide film remains intact under operational conditions; its effectiveness may be limited if the oxide layer is mechanically disrupted or if environmental conditions prevent its formation.
generation.uncertainty: While enhanced resistance is supported by corrosion and passivation data, the quantitative improvement in combined tribo-corrosion tests under realistic, dynamic wear conditions remains to be directly measured.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of MgAlTiVFeCo HEA samples sintered at various temperatures (e.g., 850 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C, and 1000 °C). Subject each sample to a standardized tribo-corrosion test that combines mechanical wear (simulating friction/abrasion) with exposure to a corrosive medium (e.g., 3.5 wt% NaCl solution) at elevated temperatures. Monitor in situ changes in passive film formation, corrosion rates, and wear depth.
measurements: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to assess passive film resistance.
Potentiodynamic polarization to measure corrosion current densities.
Surface analysis (SEM, XPS) to examine the integrity and composition of the oxide layer.
Wear quantification (e.g., profilometry) to determine tribo-corrosion degradation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 1000 °C sintered HEA (LW1000) does not exhibit a passive film resistance at least one order of magnitude higher and a significantly lower corrosion current density, along with reduced wear depth under tribo-corrosion testing compared to lower-temperature sintered samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

System: MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight high-entropy alloy (designated LW850, LW900, LW950, LW1000 based on sintering temperature). Processing: Mechanical alloying (MA) to synthesize nanocrystalline BCC solid-solution precursor powders, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 850, 900, 950, and 1000 °C. Test conditions: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution; surface morphology analysis after testing; oxidation kinetics in air at 900 °C.
